messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: optimization levels for RStan installs
parts:
On June 11, 2013 10:35:22 AM EDT, Jiqiang Guo <guo...@gmail.com> wrote:

> If following the getting started wiki, rstan would be installed under O3
> mostly. It is OK that set_cppo is not used the first time of installing
> rstan when set_cppo is not available; it uses O3 set in the package's
> Makefile.

Right. That's great. It avoids all those crazy instructions
to tweak the top-level R make config.

> For installing rstan the first time, other optimization levels
> other than O3 might be used, but it should be very rare.

What hapepns if a user

1. installs Stan,

2. sets set_cppo("debug"), and

3. reinstalls RStan?

Also, can set_cppo("debug") mess up other binary installs for user's
R packages?

Sorry to keep harping on this point, but my experience is that if there's
a way for a user to mess something up that doesn't flash warnings in
large red lights, then it's going to get messed up by at least a fraction
of the users.

Also, I have some idea how clunky the R build process is for packages.
I wish they didn't have global overrides, but I suppose that's the way R
sets most things up.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] optimization levels for RStan installs
parts:
On Tue, Jun 11, 2013 at 1:10 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:




On June 11, 2013 10:35:22 AM EDT, Jiqiang Guo <guo...@gmail.com> wrote:

> If following the getting started wiki, rstan would be installed under O3
> mostly.  It is OK that set_cppo is not used the first time of installing
> rstan when set_cppo is not available; it uses O3 set in the package's
> Makefile.

Right.  That's great.  It avoids all those crazy instructions
to tweak the top-level R make config.

> For installing rstan the first time, other optimization levels
> other than O3 might be used, but it should be very rare.

What hapepns if a user

   1. installs Stan,

   2. sets set_cppo("debug"), and

   3. reinstalls RStan?

Then it would be O0 and that is why now the wiki page has a paragraph to deal with it: 
https://code.google.com/p/stan/wiki/RStanGettingStarted#Prepare

I mean for the first time of installing rstan (no rstan is installed before), typically it would be fine since presumably 
1.)  there is no  ~/.R/Makevars. 
2.) if there is ~/.R/Makevars, typically no one messes with optimization levels.

Also, can set_cppo("debug") mess up other binary installs for user's
R packages?

Yes. Even set_cppo("fast") would change the default settings, which would change for installing all other packages and using R CMD SHLIB.  For Mac and Windows users, this is not a big problem since typically binary packages are available from CRAN.

Sorry to keep harping on this point, but my experience is that if there's
a way for a user to mess something up that doesn't flash warnings in
large red lights, then it's going to get messed up by at least a fraction
of the users.

Also, I have some idea how clunky the R build process is for packages.
I wish they didn't have global overrides, but I suppose that's the way R
sets most things up.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: optimization levels for RStan installs
parts:
On Tuesday, June 11, 2013 1:10:18 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Also, can set_cppo("debug") mess up other binary installs for user's
R packages?

It would certainly make them slower. More likely is that some other package is only tested with O2 (which is what R builds with and is the default) and doesn't work right at O3 or with O3 and NDEBUG.

Ben
